A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same PASS research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched across the figure renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on AudioMNIST, Motion Sense, and CelebA, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and attack experiments in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix F, including numerical privacy and utility measurements.

M1.justification: The stochastic substitution procedure, embedding-based probabilities, loss functions, and training and inference algorithms remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions use AudioMNIST, Motion Sense, and CelebA with identical private, useful, and hidden-useful attribute configurations and attack scenarios. The new comic introduces no evaluated task.

E2.justification: Corresponding tables retain identical comparator membership: ADV, GAP, MSDA, BDQ, PPDAR, and MaSS in the main comparisons, plus the four DP baselines and SPAct in Appendix F.3.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E retain the same splits, preprocessing, models, training budgets, NAG/mNAG metrics, and Probing Attack procedures. The larger-attacker-dataset protocol in Appendix F.2 is also unchanged.

E4.justification: The attribute-combination ablations, coefficient sweeps, substitution-set size and distribution tests, larger-attacker-data experiment, and confusion-matrix analysis are unchanged. Appendix F contains no added or removed analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three random seeds and are aggregated. The same plus/minus reporting is retained throughout the result tables, with no new uncertainty procedure or statistical test.

E6.justification: Result entries in Tables 1–5 and 7–19 and the confusion matrices are unchanged. For example, PASS mNAG remains 55.0±0.7% on AudioMNIST, 98.1±0.3% on Motion Sense, and 72.9±0.2% on CelebA in Tables 2, 4, and 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, information-theoretic formulation, Theorems 4.1–4.2 and B.1, and derivations and proofs in Appendices A–D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about adversarial-training vulnerability, PASS's theoretical foundation, and effectiveness across modalities. The comic restates the existing motivation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of privacy–utility tradeoffs, entangled attributes, and DP comparisons remain unchanged, as does Appendix G's retraining limitation. The comic supplies an illustrative restatement rather than a new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain identical, including the substitution-set settings, architectures, preprocessing, optimizer, learning rates, and training epochs in Section 5.1 and Appendix E/Table 6. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion retain the same cited works and positioning relative to adversarial privacy protection, fairness, local differential privacy, and k-l-t privacy.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short introductory sentence pointing to the new comic and its explanatory caption, and updates figure references. The remaining prose, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel comic as Figure 1; existing Figures 1–4 become Figures 2–5. The insertion reflows the main text and relocates unchanged displays, including the method overview and algorithms. Existing figure images and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Figure 1 presents the privacy goal, stronger-adversary problem, and stochastic-substitution solution in an accessible visual sequence, making the existing motivation easier to grasp. This provides a limited communication improvement; the scientific arguments, experimental evidence, proofs, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
